title: Brightness controls stop working on a monitor that has been off, asleep, or set to another input during an active session, until the session (or the PowerDevil service) is restarted
line: A DDC/CI monitor that stops answering for a while, like one set to another input, switched off or just woken up, keeps or gets back its brightness control and the brightness it missed.
explanation: When a DDC/CI brightness write still failed after the three quick retries, DDCutilDisplay marked the display as unsupported and the detector removed it; it only came back on a libddcutil connect or DPMS-awake event, which never comes for a monitor that is on another input or slow to answer after resume or power-on. When libddcutil itself had seen the monitor disappear (comment 6: -3029, then -3020 on every open), its display reference stays dead for good, and a redetection right on a wake-up event can also come too early and find nothing. Now a failed write keeps the display and is retried every 30 s for 5 minutes, so the brightness the monitor missed is written once it answers. A write that fails because the reference is dead, and a connect or awake event for a display that worked before, redetect displays, again after 2, 5, 10, 30 and 60 s while that display is still missing; the new display gets its brightness back from KWin.

commits.message:
daemon: Keep and redetect DDC/CI displays that stop answering

A monitor that stopped answering DDC/CI for a moment, like one set to
another input or just woken up, lost brightness control until powerdevil
restarted. Now writes keep retrying and lost displays get redetected.

BUG: 528077

media.caption: Master, monitor set to another input (fake DDC returns -3007, no event): a brightness key press fails after 3 retries, powerdevil removes the display, and after switching back the keys do nothing (DisplaysDBusNames empty)
Fix, same steps: after the quick retries it keeps trying every 30 s; once the input is back the missed brightness (45) is written with no key press, and the keys keep working
Master journal for the input case: 'failed to set DDC/CI brightness', 'Removing display i2c:7', 'No suitable displays detected'
Fix journal for the input case: 'retrying ... in 30000 milliseconds', then 'setvcp 10 45 -> OK' and 'succeeded to set DDC/CI brightness' after the input is back
Master, monitor stops answering and libddcutil marks its reference disconnected (comment 6: -3029, then -3020 on open): retries hit the dead reference, the display is removed and never comes back
Fix, same steps: 'lost its DDC/CI connection', displays are redetected after 2 s and 5 s, a new reference is found once the monitor answers and KWin writes the brightness back (setvcp 45 OK)
Master journal for the dead reference: '-3029', three '-3020' retries, 'Removing display i2c:7', DisplaysDBusNames 'as 0'
Fix journal for the dead reference: 'did not answer, redetecting in 2000 ms / 5000 ms', then 'Display supports Brightness' and the brightness keys work, DisplaysDBusNames 'as 1'
Master, DPMS asleep then awake event while the monitor needs a few seconds before it answers DDC/CI: the one redetection finds nothing and brightness control is gone
Fix, same steps: the monitor is redetected again after 2 s and 5 s, comes back once it answers, and the brightness keys work

review.text: Removing the permanent m_supportsBrightness = false drop on a failed DDC/CI write cleanly fixes the reported root cause, where transient communication failures (such as switching monitor inputs or resuming from sleep) permanently removed brightness controls until powerdevil restarted. Real disconnects remain handled by libddcutil events, and the patch introduces no timer, retry-counter, or lifetime hazards. The before/after logs with the fake DDC/CI harness clearly demonstrate recovery once the monitor responds again, and the separate DimDisplay-stuck-at-30% comments are appropriately left out of scope.

reviews.text: Removing the permanent m_supportsBrightness = false drop on a failed DDC/CI write cleanly fixes the reported root cause, where transient communication failures (such as switching monitor inputs or resuming from sleep) permanently removed brightness controls until powerdevil restarted. Real disconnects remain handled by libddcutil events, and the patch introduces no timer, retry-counter, or lifetime hazards. The before/after logs with the fake DDC/CI harness clearly demonstrate recovery once the monitor responds again, and the separate DimDisplay-stuck-at-30% comments are appropriately left out of scope.

All three earlier requests are resolved. The stuck-dimming variant is now fixed on master by fb6c6f6f9 (!739, which also carries BUG: 528077), so it rightly isn't duplicated. A dead libddcutil reference (-3020/-3029, c6) now triggers a queued redetection with a bounded 2-60 s backoff, only for displays that worked before. A failed write keeps the display and retries every 30 s for about 5 minutes, so the missed brightness gets applied. The fake-libddcutil journals match the captions (the reference marked dead, redetections, the display found again and setvcp 45 OK, DisplaysDBusNames back to 1). The code is careful: the connectionLost lambda captures only the id, retries and redetections are capped, and disconnect/asleep events cancel them. Nits: ddcutildetector.cpp uses std::array without including <array>. Every redetection also re-creates the healthy displays (as the existing awake path already does), and it is only verified against a fake libddcutil, not a real DDC/CI monitor.

history.text: Dropping the 'mark unsupported and remove' step after a failed DDC/CI write is the right fix for the original report (input switched away, or a write just after resume), and the fake-libddcutil rig shows the display staying listed and writable again. But the bug as titled ('off, asleep, or set to another input') and its follow-ups also cover cases this patch does not touch, as the notes admit: c7, c8 and c11 report brightness stuck at 30% dimming after the screen turns off or the system sleeps (also with DDC/CI unchecked, the DimDisplay limit left behind, MR !739), and c6 has libddcutil marking the display ref disconnected (-3020 on open) after the monitors were switched off, so keeping the display without re-opening or re-probing it won't bring control back. A write rejected after a failed undim is also never re-applied once the monitor answers, so it can stay at the wrong level until the next brightness change.
changes: Also fix the stuck-dimming-after-off/sleep variant (DimDisplay's dimming ratio not restored when the action goes away or on wake, the !739 cause) in this series with its own commit, or get the bug split so that symptom is tracked separately (e.g. under 513809) before using BUG: 528077.
Handle the c6 path: when writes fail because libddcutil considers the display ref disconnected/invalid (-3020 etc.), re-open or re-detect the display instead of keeping a dead handle, and test that.

Consider re-applying the last requested brightness/dimming the next time the display answers (or on a successful read), so an undim that failed while the monitor was away doesn't leave it at the wrong level.

history.summary: The commit now also re-detects displays whose libddcutil reference went dead (-3029/-3020) or that were missing right after a connect/awake event, with a 2-5-10-30-60 s backoff, and a failed write keeps retrying every 30 s for 5 minutes so a missed brightness is written once the monitor answers. The stuck-dimming variant was merged upstream in the meantime (fb6c6f6f9, MR !739, BUG: 528077), so it is not duplicated here.

answers.request: Also fix the stuck-dimming-after-off/sleep variant (DimDisplay's dimming ratio not restored when the action goes away or on wake, the !739 cause) in this series with its own commit, or get the bug split so that symptom is tracked separately (e.g. under 513809) before using BUG: 528077.
answers.answer: That fix landed on master after this branch's base: fb6c6f6f9 (MR !739, 2026-11-22) undims when DimDisplay is destroyed while dimmed, with 'BUG: 513809' and 'BUG: 528077' and FIXED-IN 6.8.4. A second commit doing the same would be a duplicate, so the series keeps only the DDC/CI commit. It touches only daemon/controllers/ddcutil*, applies on origin/master next to fb6c6f6f9, and keeps 'BUG: 528077' for the DDC/CI part of the title (display dropped after off, sleep or input switch).

answers.request: Handle the c6 path: when writes fail because libddcutil considers the display ref disconnected/invalid (-3020 etc.), re-open or re-detect the display instead of keeping a dead handle, and test that.
answers.answer: Done. In libddcutil 2.2.5 a reference marked disconnected is never revived (only redetection makes a working one), so re-opening can't help. The brightness worker now reports when a call fails with DDCRC_DISCONNECTED, DDCRC_INVALID_DISPLAY or DDCRC_ARG; the display logs 'lost its DDC/CI connection' and the detector redetects displays (queued, since redetection deletes the display). If the display is still missing, it redetects again after 2, 5, 10, 30 and 60 s, then stops. The same retries also run when a connect or DPMS-awake event comes for a display that had working DDC/CI before and the monitor doesn't answer yet. On the rig, a fake libddcutil reproduces comment 6's log exactly on master (-3029, then -3020 on every open, display removed, never back). With the fix the monitor comes back once it answers and KWin writes its brightness back (after-3, after-4). The early-wake case is after-5. Giving up after the last retry and a later connect event were checked too.

answers.request: Consider re-applying the last requested brightness/dimming the next time the display answers (or on a successful read), so an undim that failed while the monitor was away doesn't leave it at the wrong level.
answers.answer: Done. After the three quick retries (1, 2, 3 s), a failed write keeps its value and retries every 30 s, up to 10 more times (about 5 minutes), so it gets written once the monitor answers. A new brightness change restarts the retries with the new value. A real disconnect or sleep event removes the display and stops them. After 5 minutes it gives up but keeps the display, and the next change writes again. On the rig the missed value was written with no key press once the input was back (after-1, after-2). After a redetection, KWin re-applies its brightness to the new device. Retries are capped so a monitor that never accepts writes doesn't get DDC traffic and warnings forever.
